correctness.rationale: For birational F2-plane maps and inverses defined at all seven rational points, the degree-one group PGL3(F2) has 168 even permutations. The constructed F8-orbit quadratic involution yields double coset 1344 distinct odd permutations sending no Fano line to a line; a transposition preserves exactly 3. Noether homaloidal equations give cubic type (2,1^4), excluded because unique double base point is F2-rational. Quartic types (3,1^6) and (2^3,1^3): the former has a rational triple base point, the latter has a noncollinear degree-three Frobenius orbit of double points so a quadratic link reduces degree 4 to degree 2; product of two odd quadratic permutations is even. Infinitely near orbit exclusions and proper/noncollinear base orbit are explicitly argued. Independent GF2 computation checked group size, complete 1344 double coset, odd parity, kept-line counts 0 versus transposition count 3. Source jet programs and original outputs were read, but were not mistaken for exhaustive proof of all birational maps. No degree-five existence claimed.
residual_risks: Subtle nonstandard base-point support/infinitely-near reduction is supported by source proof, not independently formalized in a computer algebra system.
The lower bound need not be attained at degree five.
